South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 06/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, reassessment of fatigue, and evaluation of anxiety and depressive symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for his follow-up appointment, primarily to assess the management of his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and the persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. He reports minimal improvement in his dyspnea, which remains significant during exertion. He continues to use his albuterol inhaler frequently, averaging eight times daily. He states that he has been utilizing the inhaler more often during recent humid weather, which he feels aggravates his symptoms.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains unchanged, with Mr. Fairfax adhering to dietary sodium restrictions and continuing his furosemide at 80 mg daily. He notes that the edema is still 1+ pitting, particularly pronounced after prolonged periods of sitting. He denies any associated discomfort, warmth, or erythema.
Mr. Fairfax continues to experience marked fatigue, which he describes as debilitating, impacting his daily activities and social interactions. Additionally, he reports a continuation of his anxiety and depressive symptoms, with episodes of heightened anxiety correlating with his ongoing health challenges.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, continued use at eight times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 80 mg daily. 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 82, BP 130/80, RR 26, O2 sat 84% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.2, Hgb 11.0, Hct 33.0, Plt 205 2. BMP: Na 130, K 4.0, Cl 94, CO2 22, BUN 26, Cr 1.6, Glucose 92 3. BNP: 600 (further increase noted). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's dyspnea remains significant despite adherence to the inhaler regimen. A review of his inhaler technique was conducted, and he was educated on the importance of proper usage. A referral to a pulmonary rehabilitation program is strongly recommended to improve his functional capacity and address his respiratory symptoms. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema and slight increase in creatinine levels necessitate further evaluation. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage Mr. Fairfax to elevate his legs. A nephrology referral will be arranged for further evaluation given the increase in creatinine and worsening edema. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Due to the ongoing symptoms of fatigue and exacerbated anxiety/depression, a follow-up appointment with a psychologist is essential for ongoing support. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
